messages.subject: runMI warnings and fit indices
parts:
Hello everyone!
First of all, thank you for this great group. It has helped me A LOT.

I am building a model for my data, which has quite a lot missing values as well as not so big sample size (=253). Therefore I am doing sem.mi, but I receive weird warnings as well as fit indices are suspiciously good. Here is my code and summary of the results:

model2 <- '
# measurement model
    eco_outcomes =~ all_sp_box + all_m2_box + all_no_box + qlty_avg_all + eco_box_avg + weeds_all_avg
#path model
    eco_outcomes ~ box_avg_rc + s2_social_capital + s2_organization_rc
                    + s1_more_box + s2_others_location + relatedness_rc
                     + s2_damage_previous + privacy_avg_all + s2_group_meetings
                     + s2_involvement_rc + gsize_rc + s2_stability + shade_avg_all + effort_all + s1_worries_rc
                    + s2_yield_success_rc+ s2_ecoben + s2_sociben + s2_indiben
'
#runMi to fit the model
mice.eco2 <- sem.mi(model2, gb.sem1, m=20, miPackage="mice", 
                    seed=12345, estimator = "MLM")
summary(mice.eco2, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)

Convergence information:
The model converged on 20 imputed data sets

Rubin's (1987) rules were used to pool point and SE estimates across 20 imputed data sets, and to calculate degrees of freedom for each parameter's t test and CI.
Robust corrections are made by pooling the naive chi-squared statistic across 20 imputations for which the model converged, then applying the average (across imputations) scaling factor to that pooled value.
To instead pool the robust test statistics, set test = "D2" and pool.robust = TRUE.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: runMI warnings and fit indices
parts:
Robust corrections are made by pooling the naive chi-squared statistic across 20 imputations for which the model converged, then applying the average (across imputations) scaling factor to that pooled value.
To instead pool the robust test statistics, set test = "D2" and pool.robust = TRUE.
The message is just letting you know you have another option to pool the test statistic.  I appears twice because you requested fit indices, so the baseline model's chi-squared was also pooled.

Warning messages:
1: In if (attr(x, "information") == "observed") { :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used

I think I caught this in the development version.  It is a result of lavaan now accepting a vector for this argument, so different information matrices can be used for SEs than for the test statistic.  You can ignore it.

2: In cbind(c1, c2, deparse.level = 0) :
  number of rows of result is not a multiple of vector length (arg 1)

I'm not familiar with that message.

Terrence D. Jorgensen

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: runMI warnings and fit indices
parts:
The df="Inf" really is just telling you the df for that wald test is really large, so using a z distribution (instead of a t distribution) isn't a problem.

Usually if CFI = 1 and RMSEA = 0 then it means your chi-square is non-significant. Take a look at your df too. This can happen with a saturated model with 0 model df.

Alex
